title: CT HB05229: An Act Concerning Gaming.

obligations: Prohibit an individual from establishing more than one account on each electronic wagering platform operated by the licensee (Sec. 1(c)(1))

Limit a person to the use of only one debit card or only one credit card for an account, and place a monetary limit on the use of a credit card over a period of time; single-use stored value instruments purchased by cash or debit card only may be used pursuant to subdivision (3) of subsection (d) of section 12-853 (Sec. 1(c)(2))
Allow a person to limit the amount of money that may be deposited into an account, and spent per day through an account (Sec. 1(c)(3))
Provide that any money in an online account belongs solely to the owner of the account and may be withdrawn by the owner (Sec. 1(c)(4))

Establish a voluntary self-exclusion process to allow a person to exclude himself or herself from establishing an account, exclude himself or herself from placing wagers through an account, or limit the amount such person may spend using such an account (Sec. 1(c)(5))

Establish a toll-free telephone number to enable a person to receive assistance from the licensee, which may include a prerecorded message routing persons to online assistance, to resolve any problem the person is experiencing with an electronic wagering platform operated by the licensee (Sec. 1(c)(6))
Provide responsible gambling and problem gambling information to participants (Sec. 1(c)(7))

Conspicuously display on each applicable Internet web site or mobile application: a link to a description of the provisions of this subsection; a link to responsible gambling information; the toll-free telephone number established pursuant to subdivision (6); a toll-free telephone number for problem gambling; a link to information about the voluntary self-exclusion process; a clear display or periodic pop-up message of the amount of time an individual has spent; a means to initiate a break in play; and a clear display of the amount of money available in the individual's account (Sec. 1(c)(8))

State in advertising, marketing and promotional materials that individuals shall be eighteen or twenty-one years of age or older, as applicable, to participate in the type of gaming advertised, marketed or promoted (Sec. 2(e)(5))

If a direct or targeted advertisement or promotion sent to an individual, including electronic mail or text message, include a clear and conspicuous Internet link that allows the recipient to unsubscribe by clicking on one link (Sec. 2(e)(15))

Employ a geolocation system that, at a minimum, has the capacity to detect the location of a patron's device notwithstanding the use of a proxy server or virtual private network, or prohibit participation of a patron utilizing a proxy server or virtual private network (Sec. 4(b)(A))

Using industry standard technologies approved by the Department of Consumer Protection, check the location of a patron's device whenever such patron submits an entry fee for a fantasy contest or purchases a lottery draw game or keno ticket, and prohibit a patron from submitting such entry fee or making such purchase whenever the location of the patron's device is unable to be determined (Sec. 4(b)(B))

Provide a pop-up notification to a patron whenever the patron is attempting to submit an entry fee for a fantasy contest or purchase a lottery draw game or keno ticket when the location of the patron's device is unable to be determined (Sec. 4(b)(C))
Notify the online gaming operator and the patron if the patron's account is being accessed from geographically inconsistent locations (Sec. 4(b)(D))
Each lottery gaming system shall be tested and certified, in a manner and with a frequency deemed necessary by the department to preserve gaming integrity, by a gaming laboratory (Sec. 5(c)(1))

Each lottery draw game or keno shall be tested and certified, in a manner and with a frequency deemed necessary by the department to preserve gaming integrity, by a gaming laboratory prior to the corporation offering such lottery draw game or keno, with an exception for certain lottery draw games sold in at least twenty states and tested by a nationally recognized gaming testing laboratory licensed in at least twenty states (Sec. 5(c)(2))

The department may develop technical standards against which gaming laboratories shall test lottery draw games and keno for compliance; if developed, the department shall post standards on its Internet web site, review them not less than annually, may modify or update them, post updates effective thirty days after posting unless later date, and notify the corporation in writing prior to implementation (Sec. 5(c)(3))

A gaming laboratory engaged by the corporation to test and certify a lottery draw game or keno shall produce a certification report including extent of meeting technical standards, compliance with chapter and regulations, and additional information; provide the department with real-time online access to all reports through its secure communication protocol; the corporation shall submit the certification report to the department with its application for approval (Sec. 5(c)(4))

The department shall review the lottery draw game or keno being tested for proper functioning, consider test results and certification report, and may approve the lottery draw game or keno for use in the state (Sec. 5(c)(5))
The corporation shall be responsible for all costs associated with testing and obtaining certification (Sec. 5(c)(6))
prohibitions: Advertising, marketing and promotional materials shall not depict an individual who is, or appears to be, under twenty-one years of age, unless such individual is a professional athlete or a collegiate athlete who, if permitted by applicable law, is able to profit from the use of his or her name and likeness (Sec. 2(e)(1))

Shall not be aimed exclusively or primarily at individuals under twenty-one years of age, or at individuals under eighteen years of age if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof (Sec. 2(e)(2))

Shall not be published, aired, displayed or disseminated, if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof, as part of any television program aimed exclusively or primarily at individuals under eighteen years of age, or as part of any advertising, marketing or other promotional campaign interspersed during such program (Sec. 2(e)(3))

Shall not directly advertise, target or promote Internet games or retail sports wagering to specific individuals, rather than a general audience, who are excluded pursuant to a self-exclusion process, through methods including electronic mail, telephone calls, text messages, direct messaging applications, mail and social media (Sec. 2(e)(4))

Shall not contain images, symbols, celebrity or entertainer endorsements or language designed to appeal specifically to those under twenty-one years of age, or, if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof, to those under eighteen years of age (Sec. 2(e)(6))
Shall not contain inaccurate or misleading information that would reasonably be expected to confuse and mislead patrons in order to induce them to engage in gaming (Sec. 2(e)(7))

Shall not be published, aired, displayed or disseminated to a media outlet or on social media that appeal primarily to individuals under twenty-one years of age, or, if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof, to those under eighteen years of age (Sec. 2(e)(8))

Shall not be published, aired, displayed or disseminated in any athletic facility located on the campus of any public or private institution of higher education in this state, or on any Internet web site, social media platform, online service or mobile application established or maintained by or on behalf of any public or private institution of higher education in this state, unless such materials exclusively consist of an announcement, signage or display that is directed to a general audience (Sec. 2(e)(9))

Shall not be placed before any audience where the majority of the viewers or participants is presumed to be under twenty-one years of age, or, if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof, to those under eighteen years of age (Sec. 2(e)(10))
Shall not imply greater chances of winning compared to other licensees (Sec. 2(e)(11))

Shall not imply greater chances of winning based on wagering in greater quantity or amount, except for online keno and online lottery draw games that include game features approved by the department that increase the chances of winning (Sec. 2(e)(12))
Shall not contain claims or representations that gaming will guarantee an individual's social, financial or personal success (Sec. 2(e)(13))
Shall not use any type, size, location, lighting, illustration, graphic, depiction or color resulting in the obscuring of any material fact (Sec. 2(e)(14))

What it does

This act amends Connecticut gaming law to require account controls, self-exclusion, responsible gambling information, and specific website and mobile app displays for wagering licensees; imposes detailed advertising and marketing restrictions on gaming entity licensees; requires geolocation systems for fantasy contest and online lottery/keno platforms; mandates a study on prediction market platforms; and updates testing and certification requirements for lottery gaming systems and draw games or keno.

Who it applies to

  • Master wagering licensee (Sec. 1(c))
  • Licensed online gaming operator (Sec. 1(c))
  • Online gaming service provider (Sec. 1(c))
  • Sports wagering retailer (Sec. 1(c))
  • Any gaming entity licensee (Sec. 2(e))
  • Each electronic wagering platform that exclusively provides fantasy contests or sale of tickets for lottery draw games and keno through the Internet, an online service or a mobile application (Sec. 4(b))
  • Connecticut Lottery Corporation (Sec. 5(c))
  • Gaming laboratories engaged by the corporation to test and certify lottery draw games or keno (Sec. 5(c)(4))

Effective date

Sections 1 and 2 effective July 1, 2026; Sections 3, 4, and 5 effective from passage (passage date not stated in the text)

Key definitions

  • electronic wagering platform: same meaning as provided in section 12-850 of the general statutes (Sec. 4(a))
  • fantasy contest: same meaning as provided in section 12-850 of the general statutes (Sec. 4(a))
  • lottery draw game: same meaning as provided in section 12-850 of the general statutes (Sec. 4(a))
  • online gaming operator: same meaning as provided in section 12-850 of the general statutes (Sec. 4(a))
  • keno: same meaning as provided in section 12-801 of the general statutes (Sec. 4(a))

Obligations

  • Prohibit an individual from establishing more than one account on each electronic wagering platform operated by the licensee (Sec. 1(c)(1))
  • Limit a person to the use of only one debit card or only one credit card for an account, and place a monetary limit on the use of a credit card over a period of time; single-use stored value instruments purchased by cash or debit card only may be used pursuant to subdivision (3) of subsection (d) of section 12-853 (Sec. 1(c)(2))
  • Allow a person to limit the amount of money that may be deposited into an account, and spent per day through an account (Sec. 1(c)(3))
  • Provide that any money in an online account belongs solely to the owner of the account and may be withdrawn by the owner (Sec. 1(c)(4))
  • Establish a voluntary self-exclusion process to allow a person to exclude himself or herself from establishing an account, exclude himself or herself from placing wagers through an account, or limit the amount such person may spend using such an account (Sec. 1(c)(5))
  • Establish a toll-free telephone number to enable a person to receive assistance from the licensee, which may include a prerecorded message routing persons to online assistance, to resolve any problem the person is experiencing with an electronic wagering platform operated by the licensee (Sec. 1(c)(6))
  • Provide responsible gambling and problem gambling information to participants (Sec. 1(c)(7))
  • Conspicuously display on each applicable Internet web site or mobile application: a link to a description of the provisions of this subsection; a link to responsible gambling information; the toll-free telephone number established pursuant to subdivision (6); a toll-free telephone number for problem gambling; a link to information about the voluntary self-exclusion process; a clear display or periodic pop-up message of the amount of time an individual has spent; a means to initiate a break in play; and a clear display of the amount of money available in the individual's account (Sec. 1(c)(8))
  • State in advertising, marketing and promotional materials that individuals shall be eighteen or twenty-one years of age or older, as applicable, to participate in the type of gaming advertised, marketed or promoted (Sec. 2(e)(5))
  • If a direct or targeted advertisement or promotion sent to an individual, including electronic mail or text message, include a clear and conspicuous Internet link that allows the recipient to unsubscribe by clicking on one link (Sec. 2(e)(15))
  • Employ a geolocation system that, at a minimum, has the capacity to detect the location of a patron's device notwithstanding the use of a proxy server or virtual private network, or prohibit participation of a patron utilizing a proxy server or virtual private network (Sec. 4(b)(A))
  • Using industry standard technologies approved by the Department of Consumer Protection, check the location of a patron's device whenever such patron submits an entry fee for a fantasy contest or purchases a lottery draw game or keno ticket, and prohibit a patron from submitting such entry fee or making such purchase whenever the location of the patron's device is unable to be determined (Sec. 4(b)(B))
  • Provide a pop-up notification to a patron whenever the patron is attempting to submit an entry fee for a fantasy contest or purchase a lottery draw game or keno ticket when the location of the patron's device is unable to be determined (Sec. 4(b)(C))
  • Notify the online gaming operator and the patron if the patron's account is being accessed from geographically inconsistent locations (Sec. 4(b)(D))
  • Each lottery gaming system shall be tested and certified, in a manner and with a frequency deemed necessary by the department to preserve gaming integrity, by a gaming laboratory (Sec. 5(c)(1))
  • Each lottery draw game or keno shall be tested and certified, in a manner and with a frequency deemed necessary by the department to preserve gaming integrity, by a gaming laboratory prior to the corporation offering such lottery draw game or keno, with an exception for certain lottery draw games sold in at least twenty states and tested by a nationally recognized gaming testing laboratory licensed in at least twenty states (Sec. 5(c)(2))
  • The department may develop technical standards against which gaming laboratories shall test lottery draw games and keno for compliance; if developed, the department shall post standards on its Internet web site, review them not less than annually, may modify or update them, post updates effective thirty days after posting unless later date, and notify the corporation in writing prior to implementation (Sec. 5(c)(3))
  • A gaming laboratory engaged by the corporation to test and certify a lottery draw game or keno shall produce a certification report including extent of meeting technical standards, compliance with chapter and regulations, and additional information; provide the department with real-time online access to all reports through its secure communication protocol; the corporation shall submit the certification report to the department with its application for approval (Sec. 5(c)(4))
  • The department shall review the lottery draw game or keno being tested for proper functioning, consider test results and certification report, and may approve the lottery draw game or keno for use in the state (Sec. 5(c)(5))
  • The corporation shall be responsible for all costs associated with testing and obtaining certification (Sec. 5(c)(6))

Prohibitions

  • Advertising, marketing and promotional materials shall not depict an individual who is, or appears to be, under twenty-one years of age, unless such individual is a professional athlete or a collegiate athlete who, if permitted by applicable law, is able to profit from the use of his or her name and likeness (Sec. 2(e)(1))
  • Shall not be aimed exclusively or primarily at individuals under twenty-one years of age, or at individuals under eighteen years of age if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof (Sec. 2(e)(2))
  • Shall not be published, aired, displayed or disseminated, if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof, as part of any television program aimed exclusively or primarily at individuals under eighteen years of age, or as part of any advertising, marketing or other promotional campaign interspersed during such program (Sec. 2(e)(3))
  • Shall not directly advertise, target or promote Internet games or retail sports wagering to specific individuals, rather than a general audience, who are excluded pursuant to a self-exclusion process, through methods including electronic mail, telephone calls, text messages, direct messaging applications, mail and social media (Sec. 2(e)(4))
  • Shall not contain images, symbols, celebrity or entertainer endorsements or language designed to appeal specifically to those under twenty-one years of age, or, if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof, to those under eighteen years of age (Sec. 2(e)(6))
  • Shall not contain inaccurate or misleading information that would reasonably be expected to confuse and mislead patrons in order to induce them to engage in gaming (Sec. 2(e)(7))
  • Shall not be published, aired, displayed or disseminated to a media outlet or on social media that appeal primarily to individuals under twenty-one years of age, or, if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof, to those under eighteen years of age (Sec. 2(e)(8))
  • Shall not be published, aired, displayed or disseminated in any athletic facility located on the campus of any public or private institution of higher education in this state, or on any Internet web site, social media platform, online service or mobile application established or maintained by or on behalf of any public or private institution of higher education in this state, unless such materials exclusively consist of an announcement, signage or display that is directed to a general audience (Sec. 2(e)(9))
  • Shall not be placed before any audience where the majority of the viewers or participants is presumed to be under twenty-one years of age, or, if pertaining exclusively to keno, online lottery ticket sales or fantasy contests, or any combination thereof, to those under eighteen years of age (Sec. 2(e)(10))
  • Shall not imply greater chances of winning compared to other licensees (Sec. 2(e)(11))
  • Shall not imply greater chances of winning based on wagering in greater quantity or amount, except for online keno and online lottery draw games that include game features approved by the department that increase the chances of winning (Sec. 2(e)(12))
  • Shall not contain claims or representations that gaming will guarantee an individual's social, financial or personal success (Sec. 2(e)(13))
  • Shall not use any type, size, location, lighting, illustration, graphic, depiction or color resulting in the obscuring of any material fact (Sec. 2(e)(14))

Penalties and enforcement

The text does not state any penalties, fines, or a private right of action. Enforcement authority: the Department of Consumer Protection may develop technical standards, review and approve lottery draw games or keno, and may suspend a lottery draw game or keno if the department has good cause to believe that the continued operation of such game or keno could reasonably cause substantial detriment to the public interest (Sec. 5(c)(3), (5)). The Commissioner of Consumer Protection shall conduct a study and file a report (Sec. 3). No other enforcement mechanism or penalty is stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • The statute does not mention artificial intelligence or AI deployment; no AI-specific consequences are stated in the text.

Notable exemptions

  • Advertising may depict an individual under twenty-one if the individual is a professional athlete or a collegiate athlete who, if permitted by applicable law, is able to profit from the use of his or her name and likeness (Sec. 2(e)(1))
  • Advertising may imply greater chances of winning based on wagering in greater quantity or amount for online keno and online lottery draw games that include game features approved by the department that increase the chances of winning (Sec. 2(e)(12))
  • Advertising in higher education athletic facilities or on higher education websites, social media, online services or mobile applications is allowed if the materials exclusively consist of an announcement, signage or display that is directed to a general audience (Sec. 2(e)(9))
  • A lottery draw game shall not require testing and certification if the game is sold in at least twenty states within the United States and has been tested by a nationally recognized gaming testing laboratory that is licensed in at least twenty states to perform system and game analysis (Sec. 5(c)(2))
  • Single-use stored value instruments purchased by cash or debit card only, including gift cards or lottery terminal printed value vouchers, may be used pursuant to subdivision (3) of subsection (d) of section 12-853 (Sec. 1(c)(2))

Compliance steps

  • Implement account controls for each electronic wagering platform: one account per person, one debit or credit card per account with credit card monetary limits, deposit and daily spend limits, withdrawal rights, voluntary self-exclusion process, toll-free assistance number, responsible gambling information, and required website or mobile app displays (Sec. 1(c))
  • Review and revise all advertising, marketing and promotional materials to comply with age restrictions, content restrictions, no targeting of self-excluded individuals, and include an unsubscribe link in direct or targeted advertisements (Sec. 2(e))
  • If operating an electronic wagering platform that exclusively provides fantasy contests or online lottery draw games and keno, deploy a geolocation system meeting the detection, checking, pop-up notification, and inconsistent location notification requirements (Sec. 4(b))
  • If operating a lottery gaming system or offering lottery draw games or keno, arrange testing and certification by a gaming laboratory, submit certification reports to the Department of Consumer Protection, comply with any technical standards posted by the department, and pay all testing and certification costs (Sec. 5(c))
  • Monitor Department of Consumer Protection technical standards and updates, and ensure any new or modified lottery draw game or keno is tested and certified before offering (Sec. 5(c)(2), (3))

 [(12)] (14) Not use any type, size, location, lighting, illustration,

fact; and

 [(13)] (15) If a direct or targeted advertisement or promotion sent to

 Sec. 3. (Effective from passage) (a) The Commissioner of Consumer
Protection, in consultation with the office of the Attorney General, the
Mohegan Tribe, the Mashantucket Pequot Tribe and the Connecticut
Lottery Corporation, shall conduct a study concerning the effects of
prediction market platforms on the residents of this state, including, but
not limited to, the:

 (1) Use of prediction market platforms by persons under the age of
twenty-one;

 (b) Not later than February 1, 2027, the Commissioner of Consumer

 Sec. 4. (NEW) (Effective from passage) (a) As used in this section, (1)
"electronic wagering platform", "fantasy contest", "lottery draw game"

meaning as provided in section 12-801 of the general statutes.

 (b) Each electronic wagering platform that exclusively provides (1)
fantasy contests, or (2) the sale of tickets for lottery draw games and

 (A) (i) Detect the location of a patron's device notwithstanding the

 Sec. 5. Subsection (c) of section 12-806a of the general statutes is

preserve gaming integrity, by a gaming laboratory. When the
department deems such testing and certification necessary, it shall

formally notifies the department of a planned modification to the lottery

corporation immediately if it deems testing and certification of such
